column12: why

Registered as a City vendor in its own right, but the enterprise agreement is bought through Dell Marketing -- which is why the City's payments to Microsoft do not add up to what it spends on Microsoft software.
Renamed from TASER International in 2017 as body cameras and the Evidence.com platform overtook the weapons business. Sells the hardware and the evidence-management subscription together.

Three corporate owners for one product line: Intergraph Corporation was acquired by Hexagon AB, and in 2026 Hexagon spun its Safety, Infrastructure & Geospatial division out as Octave, an independent public company. The dispatch suite is now Octave I/CAD. ⚠ The City's contract is with Intergraph Corporation, two steps back; Octave itself is not a registered City vendor.
Call-recording and contact-centre software. The same platform underneath the City's separately-contracted ConvergeOne call-centre service, which is built on NICE CXone.
Same maker as the City's separately-contracted gunshot-detection system. Casebuilder is its investigation-management product, previously sold as CrimeCenter and ShotSpotter Investigate.
Renamed from ShotSpotter in 2023 as the company broadened past gunshot detection. It also makes Casebuilder, which the City buys on a separate contract -- two families here, one vendor relationship.

A public benefit corporation selling student-loan repayment advice to employers, priced per participant. The City announced the partnership itself. Not a software licence: the platform is how the advice is delivered, not the thing bought.
Privately held Canadian telematics maker. Its platform is also what the City's separate AT&T Vehicle Tracking contract runs on, so two families here share one underlying product.
Source-to-pay procurement software. This is the platform behind PASSPort, the City's own procurement system -- so the data this analysis is built from passes through a product in it.
Rebranded from ConvergeOne to C1 in 2023. It integrates and runs contact-centre systems rather than making one: the software underneath this contract is NICE CXone, which the City also buys directly.
Belgian utility billing and customer-information software, sold as UMAX and built on Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Azure -- so a Microsoft platform sits underneath this contract as well.
Citrix was taken private in 2022 and folded into Cloud Software Group alongside TIBCO. The City holds contracts under both the old and the new corporate name.

Virtual behavioural health, listed on NASDAQ since 2021. ⚠ The City's contract is with Talkspace Medical Services NY PC, a professional corporation employing licensed clinicians -- which is the clearest evidence that what is bought here is therapists' time, not a software licence.

One corporate group behind three of the City's vendors: RELX Inc, LexisNexis Risk Solutions and LexisNexis VitalChek. RELX runs LexisNexis Legal & Professional and LexisNexis Risk Solutions as separate divisions, which is why one relationship arrives on the books under several names.
Dutch street-level imagery company. It sells captured imagery as a subscription rather than a tool -- which is why this line is content the City buys, not software it runs.

Fleet and enterprise asset management software, owned by Volaris Group within Constellation Software -- an acquirer that buys and holds vertical-market software businesses, which is worth knowing when judging how a product's pricing and roadmap are likely to move.

Sells research subscriptions, Executive Programs and conference access to named users. Not a software maker: there is no product here to replace, which is why the lever on this line is the renewal date rather than a substitute.

Acquired CA Technologies in 2018 and has since raised enterprise software prices sharply across its acquisitions. ⚠ Broadcom is NOT a registered City vendor -- checked, and neither is CA Technologies -- so every dollar on this line reaches it through a reseller.

⚠ AT&T Fleet Management is Geotab's platform, resold by AT&T with AT&T's own network connectivity wrapped around it. So this family and the City's separate Geotab contracts are the same underlying product bought two ways. The two are deliberately NOT merged -- that would assert a single product identity the contract data does not carry -- but a reader comparing them should know.

Registered as a City vendor, yet none of the contracts in this family are with it: they run through Carahsoft, MTX Group and a nonprofit. The licence figure here is therefore a floor, and the unregistered citywide purchasing agreement below is the reason.
